prerequisites.title: Gusto Developer Account
prerequisites.detail: Sign up for one before filing the Production Pre-Approval application.

prerequisites.title: Security documentation
prerequisites.detail: Have audits such as SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 or PCI DSS, penetration test reports, and security and incident response contacts ready. Without a formal audit, describe practices such as background checks, MFA, encryption and data retention.

steps.title: Create Gusto Developer Account
steps.detail: Sign up for a Gusto Developer Account.
steps.done_when: You can log in to the Developer Portal.

steps.title: Draft pre-approval application and scope list
steps.detail: Draft the use-case description and a minimal scope list for the Production Pre-Approval application. Gusto assigns scopes from your use case.
steps.done_when: Draft is ready for your review.

steps.title: Submit Production Pre-Approval
steps.detail: File the application. No further action is needed until Gusto responds.

steps.title: Wait for Partnerships team decision
steps.detail: Gusto's Partnerships team reviews the application and may refuse it. If approved, the GRC team starts the Security Review.

steps.title: Assemble security review materials
steps.detail: Gather audits, penetration test reports, policies and contacts. Gusto may ask for extra information.

steps.title: Build and test in demo environment
steps.detail: Use api.gusto-demo.com for all development and test the assigned scopes there. Gusto offers no production test accounts.
steps.done_when: Integration works in demo with assigned scopes.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your Gusto client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and register it in your Gusto app.

steps.title: Wait for Security Review and QA
steps.detail: Gusto reviews security, then QA. After passing QA, it issues production credentials in the Developer Portal.

steps.title: Switch to production credentials
steps.detail: Update the auth config to the production credentials. Production calls go to api.gusto.com and assigned scopes are enforced.
steps.done_when: A test connection works against production.

traps.title: The limit is evaluated over a 60-second rolling window
traps.detail: The limit is evaluated over a 60-second rolling window per OAuth grant, so up to 200 requests are allowed in any 60-second span for each grant's access_token.

traps.title: Don't build before pre-approval
traps.detail: Gusto asks for pre-approval before you invest in the build, and it can refuse your company.

traps.title: Scopes are fixed until after launch
traps.detail: Calls outside the assigned scopes are rejected in production. Additional scopes can be requested only after release.

traps.title: No production test accounts
traps.detail: All testing, before and after launch, must happen in the demo environment.

traps.title: Rate limit is per user connection
traps.detail: The limit is 200 requests per minute per application-user pair; excess calls get HTTP 429. Plan agent call volume per connected account.

traps.title: Unified API partners don't skip review
traps.detail: Pre-Approval and Security Review are required even via an approved Unified API partner.

blockers.symptom: Production API calls rejected for a resource
blockers.what_it_means: The call is outside the scopes Gusto assigned.
blockers.what_to_do: Check granted scopes in the Developer Portal, then email Gusto to request changes after release.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the failing endpoints against the granted scope list.

blockers.what_it_means: You exceeded 200 requests in the 60-second window.
blockers.what_to_do: Back off until the window closes and spread calls across time.
blockers.agent_can_help: Add rate-limit handling and retries to the agent's Gusto calls.
